\section[\hi{शाम}]{\hi{शाम} (shaam) — "evening," and a tempting false cognate}

\label{lesson:HI-C29-shaam}



\begin{quote}
\textbf{Warm-up.} {[}PAUSE 2s{]} Last lesson's \hi{सुबह} was Persian, not Sanskrit. This word is the same story — but this time there's a Sanskrit look-alike close enough to trip you up on purpose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know — \hi{शाम} — Persian again, not Sanskrit}
\textbf{\hi{शाम}} (\textbf{shaam}) — "\textbf{evening}" — is, like \emph{subah}, a genuine \textbf{Persian} loanword: from Persian \textbf{\ar{شام}} (\emph{šām}), which traces back through \textbf{Proto-Iranian} \emph{\textbf{*xšáfnyah}} to \textbf{Proto-Indo-Iranian} \emph{\textbf{*kšápā}} ("\textbf{night}"). Hindi's two everyday time-words for "morning" and "evening" both entered the language \textbf{via Persian}, not Sanskrit — though their deeper roots differ: \emph{subah}'s traces further back to \textbf{Arabic}, while \emph{shaam}'s is native \textbf{Indo-Iranian}, a sister branch to Sanskrit itself. Persian is what they share directly; their ultimate origins are not the same.

\subsection*{You'll want to know — Be careful: a tempting, but FALSE, cognate}
Here's the trap: Sanskrit has its own word, \textbf{\hi{श्यामा}} (\textbf{śyāmā}, "\textbf{dark, night-colored}"), that \emph{looks} like it should be \emph{shaam}'s cousin — similar sound, overlapping "darkness/night" meaning, right in the neighborhood you'd expect. It \textbf{isn't}. \emph{Shaam} and \emph{śyāmā} trace to \textbf{two completely separate roots} that simply converged on similar sounds and meanings by coincidence — a genuine \textbf{false cognate}, not a shared one. Don't let the resemblance fool you into inventing a connection that isn't there.

\subsection*{Guided Practice}
{[}PAUSE 1s{]}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item {[}YOU SAY: "shaam" — "evening," another genuine Persian loan{]}
  \item {[}YOU SAY: the tempting trap — Sanskrit śyāmā looks related but ISN'T{]}
  \item {[}YOU SAY: subah and shaam — both Persian, Hindi's whole "morning and evening" pair borrowed from the same source language{]}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Wrap-up recall}]
{[}PAUSE 3s{]} Is \hi{शाम} Sanskrit or Persian? (\textbf{Persian} — from \ar{شام}, śām, like subah.) Is \hi{शाम} related to Sanskrit \hi{श्यामा} (śyāmā, "dark")? (\textbf{No} — a genuine false cognate; the resemblance is coincidental, not a shared root.) What do subah and shaam have in common, beyond both meaning a time of day? (\textbf{Both are Persian loanwords} — Hindi's morning/evening pair, unlike din/raat, isn't Sanskrit at all.)
\end{tcolorbox}
